content: 1. Store the tablets at room temperature, ensuring they are kept away from light and moisture. 2. The liquid form of this medication should be stored in the refrigerator. Do not freeze it. 3. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. 4. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. 5. This information was last revised in August 2024. 6. This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. 7. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. 8. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice and should not replace the guidance of your healthcare professional. 9. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. 10. Before taking valganciclovir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, ganciclovir, acyclovir, or any other substances. 11. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. 12. This medication may cause dizziness or drowsiness. 13. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. 14. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. 15. Limit the consumption of alcoholic beverages. 16. Valganciclovir may increase your susceptibility to infections or worsen existing infections. 17. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. 18. Inform your healthcare professional that you are using valganciclovir before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations. 19. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when absolutely necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby. 20. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. 21. Women of childbearing age should undergo a pregnancy test before starting this medication. 22. To prevent pregnancy, men with female partners should use effective barrier protection (e.g., latex or polyurethane condoms) during all sexual activity while on treatment and for at least 90 days after stopping the medication. 23. Women of childbearing age taking valganciclovir should use reliable forms of birth control (e.g., birth control pills and condoms) during treatment and for at least 30 days after stopping the medication. 24. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. 25. Due to potential risks to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. 26. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. 27. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. 28. Maintain a list of all products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 29. You may be taking other drugs that reduce bone marrow function and lower blood cell counts (e.g., cancer chemotherapy, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, zidovudine) or drugs that may cause kidney problems (e.g., cyclosporine). 30. Valganciclovir is very similar to ganciclovir. 31. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. 32. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. 33. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. 34. Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., complete blood count, kidney function, eye exams) should be conducted while taking this medication. 35. Attend all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled. 36. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. 37. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. 38.
